notes.wange: Ma comes before the noun: ma andre.

guidebook.intro: Family words and your first verbs. A verb does not change for the person: **Ma nya** I eat, **Mi nya** you eat, **Eri nya** she eats.

tips.title: Andre, ati, dede
body: **Andre** is mother, **ati** father and **dede** grandmother. The owner comes first: **ma andre** (my mother), **mi ati** (your father).
In this course a plural takes **-yi**: **buku** book, **bukuyi** books. Child and children are different words: **mva**, **anzi**.

tips.title: Ma le, ma nya, ma mvu
body: **le** want, **nya** eat, **mvu** drink, **ali** read, **imba** learn. Put the object after the verb: **Ma le ii** (I want water).
Ask **Mi le ngo?** (what do you want?): question words come at the end.

culture.title: Names
body: Many Lugbara names describe the circumstances of a birth: **Ayikoru** means joy and **Drileba** is a common boys’ name. Children are often called by a nickname at home.
